ambargo.name: Drone attack on Sheskharis oil terminal, main berths and tunnel portal hit
ambargo.note: Drones attack the "Sheskharis" oil export terminal. The main berths of the terminal and the tunnel portal of the "Grushovaya" oil depot were hit. Attribution (Nov 2026 review): SBU + GUR + GS + USF + SOF - the SBU statement of Aug 12 (card attached) says the SBU, together with the General Staff, GUR, the State Border Guard Service, the Navy and other Defense Forces components, ran the operation with drones, Palianytsia jet drones, Neptune missiles and strike systems from naval platforms; the SOF statement of Aug 12 (card attached) says SOF Deep Strike units took part together with the other components and that SOF drones reached their targets (air defense, port infrastructure and Black Sea Fleet ships); Madyar's post of Aug 12 (in sources) says the USF "Free Ukrainian Bird" also visited the naval base, the ships and the port infrastructure. The SBU statement names the Sheskharis tunnel portal directly. The existing SBU primary is kept and the other units are added. Detail (Nov 2026): the Exilenova+ analysis of Aug 12 (photos attached) says the main berths of the Sheskharis oil export terminal, including berth No. 1 used for Aframax and Suezmax tankers, were hit, and the satellite images show burn marks, a lot of firefighting foam and oil slicks in the water. The SBU statement of Aug 12 (card attached) names the tunnel portal of the "Grushova" oil depot of the Sheskharis terminal and the berths No. 3, 6 and 7 among the hit objects.

ambargo.name: Drone attack on NKHP grain terminal in Novorossiysk
ambargo.note: Drones attack the NKHP grain terminal. Grain storage facilities and transport infrastructure facilities, in particular elevators, were hit. Attribution (Nov 2026 review): SBU + GUR + GS + USF + SOF - the SBU statement of Aug 12 (card attached) says the SBU, together with the General Staff, GUR, the State Border Guard Service, the Navy and other Defense Forces components, ran the operation with drones, Palianytsia jet drones, Neptune missiles and strike systems from naval platforms; the SOF statement of Aug 12 (card attached) says SOF Deep Strike units took part together with the other components and that SOF drones reached their targets (air defense, port infrastructure and Black Sea Fleet ships); Madyar's post of Aug 12 (in sources) says the USF "Free Ukrainian Bird" also visited the naval base, the ships and the port infrastructure. This terminal is not named in the official statements; it belongs to the same night's raid on the port. The existing SBU primary is kept and the other units are added. Detail (Nov 2026): Exilenova+ (Aug 12, videos and photos attached) posted the fire at the NKHP grain terminal, the aftermath with the collapse of one of the overpasses, and a downed drone seen against the terminal wrapped in anti-drone netting; its analysis (photos attached) says numerous hits on grain stores and transport infrastructure, including elevators, are visible, and that the other two main terminals, NZT and KSK, show no damage on satellite images. The United Grain Company told the press (Aug 13, via Astra, in sources) that NKHP infrastructure was damaged.

ambargo.name: Drone attack in the NZT grain terminal area in Novorossiysk, smoke rising, terminal halts work
ambargo.note: Drones attack the NZT grain terminal. Attribution (Nov 2026 review): SBU + GUR + GS + USF + SOF - the SBU statement of Aug 12 (card attached) says the SBU, together with the General Staff, GUR, the State Border Guard Service, the Navy and other Defense Forces components, ran the operation with drones, Palianytsia jet drones, Neptune missiles and strike systems from naval platforms; the SOF statement of Aug 12 (card attached) says SOF Deep Strike units took part together with the other components and that SOF drones reached their targets (air defense, port infrastructure and Black Sea Fleet ships); Madyar's post of Aug 12 (in sources) says the USF "Free Ukrainian Bird" also visited the naval base, the ships and the port infrastructure. This terminal is not named in the official statements; it belongs to the same night's raid on the port. The existing SBU primary is kept and the other units are added. Detail (Nov 2026): Astra (Aug 12, photo attached) says its OSINT analysis found smoke rising in the area of the Novorossiysk Grain Terminal (NZT) on Portovaya Street after the night attack, and Reuters-based reports (in sources) say the terminal stopped work, but the Exilenova+ analysis (photos attached) says NZT and KSK show no damage on satellite images, so the hit on the terminal itself is unconfirmed.

ambargo.name: Drones attack tanker at oil transshipment complex in Novorossiysk
ambargo.note: Drones attack a tanker at the oil transshipment complex. Attribution (Nov 2026 review): SBU + GUR + GS + USF + SOF - the SBU statement of Aug 12 (card attached) says the SBU, together with the General Staff, GUR, the State Border Guard Service, the Navy and other Defense Forces components, ran the operation with drones, Palianytsia jet drones, Neptune missiles and strike systems from naval platforms; the SOF statement of Aug 12 (card attached) says SOF Deep Strike units took part together with the other components and that SOF drones reached their targets (air defense, port infrastructure and Black Sea Fleet ships); Madyar's post of Aug 12 (in sources) says the USF "Free Ukrainian Bird" also visited the naval base, the ships and the port infrastructure. The tanker is not named in the official statements; it belongs to the same night's raid on the port and oil infrastructure. The existing SBU primary is kept and the other units are added. Detail (Nov 2026): in_factum (Aug 13, satellite images attached) says new Vantor images show a tanker at the oil transshipment complex with an impact mark on the deck just below the bridge; the Exilenova+ analysis of Aug 12 (photos attached) says an Aframax-class tanker was probably hit while loading at Sheskharis.

ambargo.name: Drone attack on Gazprom neftekhim Salavat refinery, ELOU-AVT-4 unit on fire
ambargo.note: Drones attack the "Gazprom neftekhim Salavat" refinery. A fire was recorded and the ELOU-AVT-4 unit was reportedly burning. Attribution (Oct 2026 GS review): GS - announced by the General Staff as an operation of Defense Forces units; the executing unit was not named. Detail (Nov 2026): Astra (Aug 13, videos attached) says residents of Salavat reported smoke from the plant and the head of Bashkortostan confirmed that debris of a drone fell in the industrial zone and started a fire; Exilenova+ (Aug 13, photos attached) posted the hit on the refinery and its post of Aug 14 (photos attached) shows the plant "of yesterday" where the ELOU-AVT-4 unit was burning, preliminarily. The General Staff statement of Aug 13 (card attached) says Defense Forces units hit the complex, about 1,300 km from the border, and a fire was recorded. The source that had been in this record (Exilenova+ of Jul 16) shows the AVT-4 and AVT-6 damage from the earlier strike of Jul 14, so it was removed.

ambargo.name: Drone attack on Rosneft filling station in Volokonovka
ambargo.note: Volokonovka village, Belgorod Oblast. Drones attack the "Rosneft" filling station. A fuel dispenser is on fire. Attribution (Nov 2026 N/A review, fifth pass): none found. Belgorod's "Pepel" (Aug 13, in sources) says a drone hit the Rosneft filling station in Volokonovka and one fuel dispenser caught fire; no unit or official claim was found in the General Staff, SBU, SOF and Madyar (USF) posts of Aug 1-Sep 2 that were checked. Stays N/A.

ambargo.name: Drone attack on Wildberries logistics complex in Chishminsky
ambargo.note: Drones attack the Wildberries logistics complex. Large-scale fire on the premises of the enterprise. Attribution (Oct 2026 N/A review, fourth pass): USF - set by the analyst's rule that all Wildberries and Ozon logistics-complex attacks belong to the Unmanned Systems Forces (instruction of 20 Oct 2026); it is not taken from a unit statement about this specific attack. Confidence: rule-based (analyst instruction). Detail (Nov 2026): Astra (Aug 13, videos and photos attached) says its OSINT analysis shows the Wildberries logistics center in the Chishminsky district was attacked, and that Wildberries confirmed an air attack on the territory of an industrial zone in Bashkortostan where one of its facilities stands; Falconins (Aug 13, in sources) gives the coordinates of the hub, built on the territory of the "Center of Agrotechnologies" agro park.

ambargo.name: Chernaya Iskra partisans blow up 3 PPM tank cars in Verkhneye Dubrovo
ambargo.note: "Chernaya Iskra" partisans blow up 3 tank cars with PPM*. * The coordinates are approximate. Detail (Nov 2026): Chernaya Iskra's post of Oct 3 (claim post attached) says its agents destroyed three tank cars with 220,000 L of fuel and lubricants on Aug 13 at Kosulino station in Verkhneye Dubrovo, Sverdlovsk Oblast, a loss of more than 30 million rubles, and promises more tank-car blasts in another region. The claim was published seven weeks after the date and no independent report was found. Not independently verified.

ambargo.name: LSR partisans burn Rosgvardia vehicle in Moscow
ambargo.note: LSR partisans burn a Rosgvardia vehicle. Detail (Nov 2026): the LSR post of Aug 14 (claim post attached) says its partisans destroyed a Rosgvardia "avtozak" (prisoner van) in Moscow and links it to Rosgvardia preparations for forced "notification" raids on men of military age; the exact place in Moscow is not stated in the post. Not independently verified.

ambargo.name: Drones hit NOVATEK fractionation and hydrocracking units in Ust-Luga
ambargo.note: Drones attack port infrastructure. A stable gas condensate fractionation unit and a combined hydrocracking unit at PJSC "NOVATEK" were hit. Attribution (Oct 2026 GS review): GS - announced by the General Staff as an operation of Defense Forces units; the executing unit was not named. Detail (Nov 2026): Exilenova+ (Aug 14, photos attached) posted the aftermath of the night attack on Ust-Luga port and Astra (Aug 14, photos attached) quotes the Leningrad governor's report of a fire in the port after 51 Ukrainian drones were shot down over the region; Astra's OSINT analysis (in sources) says structures of "NOVATEK-Ust-Luga" were probably damaged. The General Staff statement of Aug 14 (card attached) says Defense Forces units hit the NOVATEK-Ust-Luga complex in Slobodka, Leningrad Oblast, with a fire recorded and two processing units preliminarily hit.

ambargo.name: Drone attack on Belneft filling station in Borisovka
ambargo.note: Borisovka urban-type settlement, Belgorod Oblast. Drones attack the "Belneft" filling station. A gas dispenser was hit. Attribution (Nov 2026 N/A review, fifth pass): none found. Kharkivskyi napriamok (Aug 14, video attached) published the footage of a drone flying into the filling station wrapped in anti-drone netting and hitting the gas dispenser, with no unit named; Belgorod's "Pepel" (Aug 14, in sources) geolocated the place on Google Maps panoramas; no unit or official claim was found in the General Staff, SBU, SOF and Madyar (USF) posts of Aug 1-Sep 2 that were checked. Stays N/A.

ambargo.name: Drone attack on Savasleyka airfield where MiG-31Ks are based
ambargo.note: Drones attack an airfield where "MiG-31K" aircraft are based. Attribution (Nov 2026 review): GS - the General Staff statement of Aug 15 (card attached) names the Savasleyka airfield directly and announces the strike as an operation of Defense Forces units; the executing unit was not named. Detail (Nov 2026): the General Staff statement of Aug 15 (card attached) says Defense Forces units hit the Savasleyka airfield in Nizhny Novgorod Oblast, with a hit on the target and a fire on the airfield territory, and that the airfield is used to base and operate MiG-31K interceptors, carriers of Kinzhal aeroballistic missiles. No photo or video of the strike itself was found.

ambargo.name: Flamingo missile strike on RKTs Progress in Samara
ambargo.note: FP-5 "Flamingo" missile strike on RKTs "Progress". Fire on the premises of the enterprise. Attribution (Nov 2026 review): GS - the General Staff statement of Aug 15 (card attached) says Defense Forces units hit the Progress rocket and space center in Samara, with a hit on the target and a fire on the site; President Zelensky also confirmed the strike as an operation of the Defense Forces. The executing unit was not named. Detail (Nov 2026): Exilenova+ (Aug 15, videos attached) posted the first reports of a Flamingo arrival and several videos of the moment of impact in Samara; its analysis (photo attached) says the FP-5 "Flamingo" cruise missile strike probably hit building 106A of the Soyuz production area (53.217623, 50.303163), where onboard electronics are assembled, next to the final assembly building 106B. The governor of Samara Oblast confirmed a missile strike on the enterprise, not drone debris (Exilenova+, Aug 15, in sources).

ambargo.name: Drone attack on Wildberries logistics complex in Koledino
ambargo.note: Drones are attacking the Wildberries logistics complex. A large-scale fire on the premises of the enterprise. Attribution (Oct 2026 GS review): GS - Ukrainian Ministry of Defence confirmed the strike (Defense Forces drones); executing unit not named. Attribution (Oct 2026 N/A review, fourth pass): USF - set by the analyst's rule that all Wildberries and Ozon logistics-complex attacks belong to the Unmanned Systems Forces (instruction of 20 Oct 2026); it is not taken from a unit statement about this specific attack. It replaces the earlier GS attribution quoted above. Confidence: rule-based (analyst instruction). Detail (Nov 2026): Exilenova+ (Aug 16, videos attached) posted the burning Wildberries warehouse in Koledino together with the Severnoye Domodedovo complex, and its post of Aug 16 (in sources) says the Koledino logistics center, 229,500 sq m and the company's largest hub, was hit at 55.386345, 37.584193.

ambargo.name: Drone attack on Severnoye Domodedovo logistics complex
ambargo.note: Drones are attacking the "Severnoye Domodedovo" logistics complex. A large-scale fire on the premises of the enterprise. Attribution (Nov 2026 N/A review, fifth pass): none found. Exilenova+ (Aug 16, videos attached) posted the burning multimodal logistics complex "Severnoye Domodedovo" together with the Wildberries hub in Koledino, and its post of Aug 16 (in sources) says a warehouse of 51,700 sq m at 55.473179, 37.723962 was hit; no unit or official claim was found in the General Staff, SBU, SOF and Madyar (USF) posts of Aug 1-Sep 2 that were checked. Stays N/A.

ambargo.name: Drone attack on Kombinat Kamensky defense plant
ambargo.note: Drones are attacking the defense enterprise FKP "Kombinat Kamensky". Attribution (Oct 2026 GS review): GS - announced by the General Staff as an operation of Defense Forces units; the executing unit was not named. Detail (Nov 2026): the General Staff statement of Aug 16 (card attached) says Defense Forces units hit the "Kombinat Kamensky" plant in Kamensk-Shakhtinsky, Rostov Oblast, which makes solid rocket fuel for Uragan, Smerch and Tornado-S rocket munitions, with a fire recorded on the site; the follow-up of Aug 17 (photos attached) confirms the destruction of two workshops and damage to four more workshops making explosives and powders. The Rostov authorities opened a hotline for those hurt in the drone attack (Astra, Aug 17, in sources). The USF commander's summary of Aug 24 lists the plant too, but that entry belongs to the second strike of Aug 24 (a separate record).

ambargo.name: Drones hit mobile fire group pickup in Grayvoron
ambargo.note: Drones are attacking a pickup truck of a mobile fire group. Attribution (Nov 2026 N/A review, fifth pass): none found among the listed strike units. Belgorod's "Pepel" (Aug 17, video attached) says the video was published on Aug 16 by the 105th Separate Territorial Defense Brigade; one drone hit the pickup of a mobile fire group and a second hit the cellular antenna, and the place was geolocated from the objects in the video and satellite images. This is a brigade-level unit, not one of the strike units used in this tab; no unit or official claim was found in the General Staff, SBU, SOF and Madyar (USF) posts of Aug 1-Sep 2 that were checked. Stays N/A.

ambargo.name: Drones destroy cellular antennas in Grayvoron
ambargo.note: Drones are destroying cellular communication antennas. Attribution (Nov 2026 N/A review, fifth pass): none found among the listed strike units. Belgorod's "Pepel" (Aug 17, video attached) says the video was published on Aug 16 by the 105th Separate Territorial Defense Brigade; one drone hit the pickup of a mobile fire group and a second hit the antenna on the cellular tower, and the place was geolocated from the objects in the video and satellite images. This is a brigade-level unit, not one of the strike units used in this tab; no unit or official claim was found in the General Staff, SBU, SOF and Madyar (USF) posts of Aug 1-Sep 2 that were checked. Stays N/A.

ambargo.name: Drone attack on Bashneft-UNPZ refinery in Ufa, AVT-6 hit
ambargo.note: Drones are attacking the "Bashneft-UNPZ" refinery. The AVT-6 unit has been hit. Attribution (Nov 2026 N/A review, fifth pass): none found. Militarnyi and Censor.net (Aug 19, in sources) say drones hit the AVT-6 unit of Bashneft-UNPZ in the second attack on an Ufa refinery in two days, with a fire at the unit; no unit or official claim was found in the General Staff, SBU, SOF and Madyar (USF) posts of Aug 1-Sep 2 that were checked. Stays N/A.

ambargo.name: Airstrike on electrical substation in Shebekino
ambargo.note: Airstrike on an electrical substation. Power outage in the city and surrounding settlements. Attribution (Nov 2026 N/A review, fifth pass): the GS attribution made in the Oct 2026 N/A review is withdrawn. It was inferred, with low confidence, only from the weapon class (an air-launched munition is operated by the Air Force), and no Ukrainian unit or official claim was found. Belgorod's "Pepel" (Aug 19, in sources) says an electrical substation is burning in Shebekino after an airstrike, with a huge column of black smoke over the city. Stays N/A.

ambargo.name: Atesh partisans destroy communications tower in Malaya Loknya
ambargo.note: Partisans of "Atesh" are destroying a communications tower*. * Probable location of the sabotage. Detail (Nov 2026): the Atesh post of Aug 19 (claim post attached) says its agents destroyed three communications towers near Daryino, Malaya Loknya and Sverdlikovo in the Kursk direction, which carried closed channels linking the command posts of the 83rd Separate Guards Air Assault Brigade and the 1443rd Motor Rifle Regiment. The post does not say which tower is which, so the location is the probable place near Malaya Loknya. Not independently verified.

ambargo.name: Fire at VNIIR-Progress electrical substation in Cheboksary
ambargo.note: The "VNIIR-Progress" electrical substation is on fire. Attribution (Nov 2026 N/A review, fifth pass): none found. Exilenova+ (Aug 19, videos attached) posted the burning substation and Astra (Aug 19, videos attached) confirmed with OSINT analysis that the substation on the territory of the "VNIIR-Progress" plant, which makes drone components and antennas, caught fire; the mayor confirmed an incident at the substation on Yakovlev Avenue and the local media reported an explosion sound and a fire at noon, with no cause given. no unit or official claim was found in the General Staff, SBU, SOF and Madyar (USF) posts of Aug 1-Sep 2 that were checked. Stays N/A.

ambargo.name: Drones attack Su-34 bomber in Akhtubinsk
ambargo.note: Drones are attacking a Su-34 bomber. Attribution (Nov 2026 review): GS - the General Staff statement of Aug 21 (card attached) confirms the strike of Aug 20 on the Akhtubinsk airfield and the damaged Su-34 as an operation of Defense Forces units; the executing unit was not named. Detail (Nov 2026): Exilenova+ (Aug 20, photo attached) reported an attack of unknown drones on Akhtubinsk and a thermal signature near the air defense of the airfield; the General Staff statement of Aug 21 (card attached) confirms damage to a Su-34 and a fuel spill on the territory of the airfield, home of the 929th State Flight Test Center and of Su-34 bombers that drop guided bombs on Ukraine, about 650 km from the front line.

ambargo.name: Drone attack on TANECO refinery in Nizhnekamsk, fire on site

Attribution (Oct 2026 N/A review): USF + SOF - credited in the USF commander's September 2026 strike list (Telegram post of 26 Sep): Tolyattikauchuk, 12 Sep, 1st Separate Center with SOF. SOF's own Telegram post of 12 Sep names its Deep Strike units jointly with the USF. Confidence: high. Detail (Nov 2026): Exilenova+ (Sep 12, videos attached) posted fires and the moment of an arrival in Tolyatti during the night attack, first described by locals as an attack on the KuibyshevAzot chemical plant; its post of Sep 15 (photo attached) says the strike set the BK-2, BK-3 and BK-4 shops of Tolyattikauchuk on fire, the units for butyl rubber and the isobutane-isobutylene fraction. The General Staff statement of Sep 12 (card attached) says Defense Forces units hit the plant, with a hit and a fire, and the SOF statement of Sep 12 (card attached) says the SOF Deep Strike units hit it together with the Unmanned Systems Forces.

ambargo.name: Atlant Aero drone storage warehouse destroyed in Taganrog

Detail (Nov 2026): Exilenova+ (Sep 12, videos attached) relays the SBU report with footage, and Exilenova+ (Sep 12, in sources) names the Atlant Aero enterprise, which designs and builds strike and reconnaissance drones. The General Staff statement of Sep 15 (in sources) says explosions and a fire were recorded at Atlant Aero in the night of Sep 15, so the enterprise was hit again three days after this record; that strike has its own record ("Missile strike on Atlant Aero drone plant in Taganrog").

ambargo.name: Airstrike destroys logistics hub and drone lab in Shebekino
ambargo.note: An airstrike destroys a logistics hub and a UAV laboratory. Attribution (Nov 2026 N/A review, fifth pass): the GS attribution made in the Oct 2026 GS review is withdrawn. It rested on a Censor.NET headline crediting the Air Force, which is not a unit used in this tab, and no General Staff statement was found. The Kharkiv Direction channel (Sep 13, video attached) says Ukrainian intelligence found that the command of the 128th Separate Motor Rifle Brigade of the 44th Army Corps had set up a logistics hub and a UAV assembly and tuning laboratory, Molniya drones included, in a shop of the Shebekino Karton plant, and that a strike with guided bombs destroyed two UAV test engineers and a large amount of equipment from the warehouse; Belgorod's Pepel (Sep 13, in sources) says the Gofrotara cardboard plant came under an airstrike and confirms the location by geolocation. no unit or official claim was found in the General Staff, SBU, SOF and Madyar (USF) posts of Sep 1-Oct 3 that were checked. Stays N/A.

Detail (Nov 2026): Astra (Sep 13, videos attached) posted the burning refinery with an OSINT analysis and noted that no official report had yet been made; Exilenova+ (Sep 13, videos and photos attached) says Defense Forces strike drones hit it in the night with a large fire in the industrial zone. Dnipro Osint (Sep 13, photo attached) and Exilenova+ (Sep 13, in sources) relay the GUR statement that operators of the GUR Active Actions Department and the GUR Unmanned Systems Department hit the refinery in a joint deep-strike operation with the Defense Forces. ambargo.name: Missile strike on Ozon warehouse in Taganrog
ambargo.note: Missile strike on the Ozon warehouse. Attribution (Oct 2026 N/A review): GS - inferred from the weapon class only (missile / HIMARS / air-launched munition is operated by the Missile Troops and Artillery, Air Force or Navy); the strike is known mainly from Russian-side reports and no Ukrainian unit or official claim was found. Confidence: low. Attribution (Oct 2026 N/A review, fourth pass): USF - set by the analyst's rule that all Wildberries and Ozon logistics-complex attacks belong to the Unmanned Systems Forces (instruction of 20 Oct 2026); it is not taken from a unit statement about this specific attack. Detail (Nov 2026): Astra (Sep 15, video and photos attached) relays the Rostov governor and the mayor of Taganrog, who describe a massive missile attack on the city with a fire at the Ozon warehouse and agricultural warehouses, so the record keeps the missile method from these Russian reports. The missile reading is kept after a further check: the General Staff weekly summary of Sep 21 (in sources) confirms a strike on Atlant Aero in Taganrog in the night of Sep 15, and Exilenova+ satellite imagery (relayed by Militarnyi and Ukrainska Pravda, Sep 18) shows three production buildings of Atlant Aero destroyed by Neptune missiles; the Ozon warehouse of this record lies less than 1 km from the Atlant Aero site, so it was probably damaged in the same missile strike. desk.text:
Dobropillia direction - situation analysis 🇺🇦/🇷🇺
For months, the Russian army has been concentrating its forces and strikes on the Dobropillia direction, with the aim of capturing the city.
Here is a full analysis on what is happening there :
🧵THREAD🧵1/17 ⬇️

thread.text:
Every source available to me confirms the same picture: the manpower Russia has committed to this front is staggering.
We are talking about hundreds of Russian soldiers killed every day, and an unprecedented concentration of four combined arms armies (CAAs) on a 50 km front.

This map shows the current situation on the front, as mapped by DeepState, including the area captured in 2026 and the grey zone. I have also added the Russian and Ukrainian units deployed in the area.
Generally, the map is quite accurate, even if I have a bigger grey zone.

Russian mappers have a very different picture, for them, Dobropillia fell already and everything is under their control.
This is done under Russian MOD pressure (hence the large grey zone) and only represents the maximal infiltration area.

In recent weeks, I've seen multiple accounts/soldiers saying the same thing, Russian losses are very high because they are using many men.
Many soldiers dying are not killed during infiltration or offensive but during the walk to frontline positions.

Many other comments come to confirm this, from both soldiers and journalists.
After his trip in the region, @JulianRoepcke said : "Ukraine inflicts ten times as many casualties on Russia as it sustains itself. In certain sectors of the front, this ratio reaches as high as 40:1.
Most Russian soldiers who reach the "kill zone"—the final 25 kilometers—are killed there."

To prove that, I will show you 8 different videos gathered by @Exilenova_plus showing Russian logistic routes in the Dobropilla area.
There is a constant threat and destroyed vehicles are everywhere.
On this video, we can see some (not that unusual) horses used for logistics, together with small vehicles.
On this one, a Russian soldier walks among dead bodies (I've found many videos with dead bodies but I prefer not to share those).

On this one, Russian soldiers heading to the frontline in the fog are being attacked by a Ukrainian FPV drone, exploding nearby.
The second one shows a logistic run last summer under FPV drone threat. You can understand why it's easier to hide in summer...
Just a look at what the @usf_army are doing show the losses are increasing. Also, take a look at the casualities ratio. We are close to a 1:1 killed/wounded...

3 drone units are active mostly in this exact direction,
▫️414th Magyar birds (5 200 soldiers hit this month)
▫️K2 (1 700 soldiers hit this month)
▫️Feniks (3 900 soldiers hit this month)
In total, hundreds of Russian soldiers are hit by drones everyday there.

If you follow me, you may remember I followed Russian KAB strikes. For months, Russia has been launching thousands of KABs at Dobropilla and neighbouring areas.
On this map, you can see where they concentrate themselves.

Here is an animated maps of Russian KAB strikes in Donbas this year, showing how they concentrate firepower there.
Many times, I've read that there are constant FPV strikes and artillery shelling.

I've recently followed those, but Russia is increasingly using armoured vehicles to launch assault operations in the region, particularly during foggy weather.
Most assaults fail before reaching the frontline but partly succeed in bringing many men forward.

For the precise situation, I will quote @Playfra0's words :
"Dobropillia direction.
Contrary to all claims hinting otherwise, Ukrainian forces continue holding positions in a defensive perimeter all around Dobropillia (yellow lines, illustrative) and everywhere in Dobropillia itself.
Regarding Russian infiltrations into Dobropillia itself, information contained in corresponds to reality: Russian infiltrator presence in the city is minuscule compared to the Ukrainian presence at the moment of writing, other than being by itself very small.
There is no single area where the few Russian infiltrators are particularly concentrated; they're rather scattered, being unable to accumulate critical mass anywhere despite continued strong efforts to do so.
This is likely thanks to combined effort and appropriate cooperation between different Ukrainian units with the elimination of Russian infiltrators through indirect means, as well as direct periodical infantry clearings.
Meanwhile, without direct confirmation from my part, it's still likely that the Russians conserve the ability to infiltrate Dobropillia itself and generally continue doing so through the usual already known routes approximately marked with the red arrows.
In general, I'd describe the situation as very difficult and subject to change, but for now stable."

Overall, the situation remains very difficult, with a slow Russian progress this year that threatens the city.
I will continue to particularly follow the tactical situation here.
Thanks for following.

thread.text: 2/ The 218th Guards Tank Regiment (unit 82588) is part of the 27th Motor Rifle Division (unit 44980) of the 5th Combined Arms Army (unit 06426). It is commanded by Guards Lieutenant Colonel Petr Andreevich Zyblev. The 'Guards' designation indicates exceptional combat performance.

3/ The Primorsky Krai-based regiment has been fighting since the February 2022 full-scale invasion. It has been engaged in operations on Ukraine's southern front in the Zaporizhzhia/southern Donetsk sector.

4/ An officer with the regiment has reportedly leaked photographs showing men who went AWOL being punished by being handcuffed to trees and left without food for several days. They are held until they agree to join assaults, in which many have died.

5/ The soldiers reportedly refuse to carry out combat missions that they consider to be a "one-way ticket," leave their positions, and do not return. In the past three months, 43 soldiers from the regiment have gone AWOL: 18 in August, 14 in September, and 11 in October 2026.

6/ Leaked detailed lists of the regiment's losses indicate that it has sustained nearly 5,000 casualties, including deaths, missing persons, wounded, and those who have gone AWOL. The regiment's nominal strength is 2,010 personnel. Dozens of officers have been killed or injured.
7/ The documents indicate that most of them died as a result of attacks by FPV drones. Among the deceased are 31 junior and senior officers.

8/ An additional 1,330 personnel are listed as missing, including 22 officers. According to the documents, in most cases this is likewise a result of attacks by FPV drones.
The detailed list of wounded includes 1,163 personnel, including 60 officers.

9/ In addition, 326 personnel are listed as AWOL, including 5 officers. The documents record that approximately 90 did not return from leave, a small number deserted from training grounds, and the rest left directly from their positions.
10/ According to the officer who leaked the documents, the principal reasons for desertion are the regiment's heavy losses, constant "meat assaults," extortion, and low levels of provision.
11/ In total, the four lists contain 4,924 entries regarding the deceased, missing, wounded, and AWOL personnel. This is equivalent to 245% of the regiment's nominal strength of 2,010 personnel.

12/ The ratio of killed to wounded is extremely high – 2,105 personnel killed, 95 more than the regiment's entire nominal strength, compared to 1,163 wounded, representing a ratio of 1.8 killed for every 1 wounded.

13/ If the missing are considered to be dead too (which is more than likely), the ratio climbs as high as 2.8 killed for every 1 wounded. The extremely high ratio likely reflects a combination of inability to evacuate and poor or nonexistent frontline medical care.

14/ These figures indicate that the personnel of the 218th Regiment have been effectively replaced multiple times due to the high losses. At the same time, according to the officer, the unit's command continues to send soldiers on "meat assaults" even after such losses.

15/ The life expectancy of soldiers with the regiment can be extremely short. Three men from the unit are reported to have been killed in a drone strike within as little as 24 hours of signing a contract to join the army, suggesting that they were deployed without any training.

16/ Wounded soldiers have also complained of being sent to the front on crutches and of being denied medical treatment. After one man was badly wounded in an explosion, he went to a nearby position to seek treatment but was thrown into a pit instead and threatened with execution:

17/ "They shoved me into a hole and started threatening to kill me: 'We're going to shoot you now, we're going to shoot you.' I stayed there until half past six in the morning, after which they started sending me back to my position."

18/ Videos leaked from the regiment show commanders similarly threatening their men with execution if they refuse to join assaults. A 2025 video shows the commander of the "V" assault company, Yuri Babakov, call sign "Pitersky," threatening recalcitrant soldiers with reprisals.

19/ During a briefing, Babakov told the soldiers that if they failed to comply with the order, he would personally execute them and report them to command as missing in action. According to the commander, he had permission from his superiors to kill them:

20/ “If you don’t follow orders, if you refuse to do your jobs, I swear on my mother’s life, I swear on my children’s lives, I’ll personally shoot you. Every single one of you ... You’re all in this mess, you fucking animals—except for that one guy. You’re all animals.” /end

Major hacking incident:
Hackers from Belarus and Ukraine were able to retrieve data from the Russian Federal State Statistics Service "ROSSTAT", the main statistics agency of Russia, headquartered in Moscow.
ROSSTAT collects, analyzes, and publishes official data on the country's economy, demographics, environment, and social developments. It also collects death toll data, including those fallen in Russia's war in Ukraine.
The Belarusian opposition group "Cyber Partisans" and the pro-Ukrainian group "Silent Crow" were able to retrieve a large volume of data. The news portal "Mediazone" peer-checked the data and confirms high probability in its authenticity.
According to reports by Bloomberg, the groups stated on November 1, 2026, that they had infiltrated roughly 25,000 computers within Rosstat's internal infrastructure and extracted around 23 terabytes of data, including millions of civil registry death records.

The methodology:
Mediazona had access to the entire database, which, combined with other data sources they already had previously, made it possible to deanonymize 10.1 million of the 11.6 million deaths since 2021.
The data leak was therefore confirmed both by inheritance declarations and the data available for 2021.
Before commenting, it is better to read the article:

“What if we injected hundreds of thousands of military deaths into the real data?
There are two arguments against this: the structure of the data itself and verification with the inheritance register and other external sources. The former makes data injection very difficult, while the latter makes it virtually impossible.
Each death record has a unique record number; in the database this field is called fact_id, as mentioned earlier in the data processing section. Its format is defined by Order No. 202n of the Ministry of Finance. This number includes the type of registration (7 – death), the year of creation, the civil registry office number, the serial number of the registration in that office for the year concerned, and a check digit."
Graphic -> @mediazona_en

Mediazona was also able to verify that the figures correspond to those of the inheritance, this is further confirmation of the authenticity of the figures.
They also compared thousands of individuals they haven't published yet and it matches.
Graphic -> @mediazona_en

In total, Mediazona therefore found 490,000 dead in the war, including:
▫️425,000 killed “in war” (it was 390,000 for the hackers who only analyzed until August)
▫️43,000 declared dead in court
▫️21,000 Others
Graphic -> @mediazona_en translated

Please note, they only counted male Russian citizens aged 18 to 64 killed in the war in Ukraine. This excludes the few errors.
Losses of the Donetsk and Luhansk People's Republics are absent from Rosstat data, as are foreign deaths in the Russian army.
Civilians killed in combat zones were also withdrawn.

Mediazona also discusses the deadline for recording losses.
“The longer the war drags on, the more military deaths are recorded after a year or even more: for example, the graph shows that Rosstat may not yet have reached the year 2025. This means that the data from the end of September (however reliable and accurate it may be) does not reflect the real number of casualties.”

Finally, Mediazona looks back at length on those missing in action and reveals many details.
In total, they estimate 530,000 deaths by the end of 2025 (their previous count was 350,000) and estimate that this figure should reach 720,000 by the end of fall 2026.

Now that everything is public, we have confirmation of the authenticity of the data leak and the analysis of information.
Anyone curious can download the entire file revealed by @cpartisans today:

Another media outlet (@istories_media) also had access to the same data.
They come to the same conclusion, around 490,000 Russian soldiers were killed and estimate that this figure would reach at least 620,000 (they do not have the same count of MIAs).
Their graphs are very interesting, for example this one which confirms my previous figures of 700 deaths per day, as was the case during several months of 2025.
They also have a map of the location of Russian soldiers killed during the war. I advise you to fly over certain districts, for example Sudja (12,000), Pokrovsk (50,000), or Lyman (15,000).

Ultimately, the numerous criticisms received in recent weeks for highlighting the work of @M0nstas which showed exactly the same thing proves that I was right.
The obsession of some to refuse to accept the reality of Russian losses - as well as Ukrainian ones - betrays their lack of objectivity and raises questions about their impartiality.

desk.text:
Rosstat data revealed the death of almost 500 thousand people in the war - and this data is real. Taking into account the missing, the figure today is about 700 thousand
By the end of September 2026, at least 490 thousand people had died in the war with Ukraine - these are people whose deaths have already been registered and are visible in the data from the Rosstat hack, which were provided to journalists by Belarusian and Ukrainian hackers (“CyberPartisans” and Silent Crow).
We are confident that this data is real: it is verified by the name list of the dead (including not yet published records), the Register of Inheritance Cases, other registry office leaks, texts of court decisions from open sources and previously published data from Rosstat itself.
Also, thanks to Rosstat, we were able to double-check our previous estimates of losses according to the Register of Inheritance Cases - and found out that they were quite accurate or even underestimated in terms of missing persons.
Taking into account delays in registering deaths, the real death toll for September, according to our estimate, is about 700 thousand people.
This is a joint text with Meduza as part of our mortality assessment project. The list of victims by name is the work of Mediazona, the BBC Russian Service and a team of volunteers.

Russia's courts are declaring its missing soldiers dead, but new cases keep joining a backlog that shows no sign of being cleared.
The Rosstat leaks show that these deaths are not processed year by year. Every month, courts declare men dead who disappeared in 2025, 2024, and even 2023 or 2022. The number entering the register grew through 2025 and into spring 2026, then levelled off at around 2,000 a month.
As cases from 2025 take up more of that capacity, older cases take up less. But they haven't been cleared. New cases simply join the same pile.
The delay is substantial. Men registered in 2025 or 2026 had died about 14 months earlier on average: roughly 11 months before the court ruling and another two before registration. Half waited between 11 and 18 months.
Meanwhile, the missing from 2026 have barely begun to appear. The courts are still processing deaths from 2024 alongside those from 2025, while another year's cases accumulate.
No year is cleared before the next joins the pile. With registrations holding at around 2,000 a month and the war continuing to produce missing men, there is no sign of the backlog coming to an end.

War Beyond Ukraine: Where and How Ukrainian Forces Are Countering Russian Military Influence in the Middle East and Africa
I came across an interesting post by prominent French OSINT analyst Clément Molin, who described attacks on Russian forces in Libya as “Ukraine’s Mediterranean Front.”
That inspired me to put together an overview of other places where Ukraine has established its own unofficial “fronts” thousands of kilometers beyond its borders.
🇸🇩 Sudan — Reports of Ukrainian special forces operating alongside the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) against the Rapid Support Forces (RSF), a paramilitary group linked to Russia’s Wagner PMC.
🇲🇱 Mali — Ukrainian intelligence cooperation with Tuareg rebels fighting against Mali’s government forces and Russia’s Africa Corps.
🇱🇾 Libya — Reports of Ukrainian naval drone operators operating in the country and conducting operations against Russian military interests.
🇸🇾 Syria — Reports of Ukrainian intelligence supporting Syrian rebels and conducting operations against Russian forces in 2024.
Ukrainian forces will continue training Russia’s adversaries in drone warfare, sharing their experience in modern combat, conducting intelligence operations, and striking Russian military interests.
As long as Russia continues its war against Ukraine, its military presence abroad may also become part of this confrontation.

Situation on the Orikhiv direction, Zaporizhzhia Oblast:
Over the last week, heavy fighting continued in the Orikhiv direction, with both Russian and Ukrainian forces launching extensive assault operations across the frontline.
In the west, Ukrainian forces once again regained control over the fields north of Mali Shcherbaky and are working to clear out additional Russian positions in the fields there. Russian forces are continuing their infiltration attempts to the west and east, as well as northeast towards Yurkivka and the treelines northeast of Shcherbaky.
To the southeast, Russian forces continued their infiltration attempts towards the forest southwest of Novopavlivka, with some small groups even managing to enter the village itself where Ukrainian forces are attempting clearing operations. Russian assault groups are also continuing their storming operations on Novoandriivka, attacking from the west and south, while simultaneously attempting to clear Ukrainian treeline positions west and southeast of the village. In addition to this, Russian forces are attacking along the road from Nesteryanka towards Orikhiv, engaging in clashes with Ukrainian forces near the highway intersection.
To the east, Ukrainian forces continued their counterattacks in the central and southern parts of Novodanylivka, although their rate of advance has slowed as they reach more solidified Russian positions.…

Situation on the Pokrovs'ke and Velyka Novosilka directions, Donetsk/Dnipropetrovsk Oblasts:
Over the last few weeks, positional battles continued near the Donetsk-Dnipropetrovsk regional border, with both Russian and Ukrainian forces carrying out limited assault operations in different areas.
In the southwest, Russian forces cleared out the earlier Ukrainian infiltrations west of Uspenivka, and are working to re-establish control over the rest of Solodke, where Ukrainian forces are actively counterattacking. Russian infiltration attempts through the large grey-zone towards Zlahoda from the southwest are also continuing.
To the northeast, Ukrainian forces cleared out the earlier Russian infiltrations into Verbove, re-establishing control over the village and its surroundings. Russian forces conducted assault operations near Krasnohirske and attempted infiltrations into the Pryvillya area along the eastern bank of the Yanchur River.
To the east, the Russians continued limited assault operations west of Novomykolaivka and south of Kalynivske, while Ukrainian forces occasionally attempt to advance towards Novohryhorivka from the north. Additionally, Russian forces cleared part of Zaporizke from earlier Ukrainian infiltrations, while Ukrainian assault groups are sporadically attacking the Berezove, Zaporizke, Novoheorhiivka, and Komyshuvakha areas.
+ ~7.89 km² in favour of Ukraine.
+ ~5.79 km² in favour of Russia.

Situation on the Dobropillya and Druzhkivka directions, Donetsk Oblast:
Over the last week, both Russian and Ukrainian forces have been conducting assault operations on the banks of the Kazenyi Torets River, each attacking in different areas.
In the west, Ukrainian forces cleared out the earlier Russian infiltrations south of Zolotyi Kolodyaz and north of Kucheriv Yar, and re-established control over positions in most of Kucheriv Yar. Russian forces continued their assaults towards Kucheriv Yar from the south, but have so far been unable to make any significant progress. A Russian mechanised assault was also carried out along the road to Hruzke, with several groups of infantry dismounting north and northwest of Shakhove where they are attempting to consolidate. Fighting continues for the forest north of Shakhove, where several advanced Ukrainian positions remain.
To the northeast, Russian forces continued occasionally crossing the Hruzka River into Novomykolaivka, where they engage in sporadic clashes with Ukrainian forces in the grey-zone there. Renewed Russian assaults are also being carried out on Novohryhorivka, as well as east into the Raiske area.
+ ~6.81 km² in favour of Ukraine.

Situation on the Lyman direction, Donetsk Oblast:
Over the last couple of weeks, Ukrainian forces continued their counteroffensive operations west and east of the Zherebets River, while Russian forces carry out a new series of deep infiltration operations.
In the north, Ukrainian forces continued their gradual advance in Zarichne, slowly clearing the village block-by-block amid fierce Russian resistance. Forward Ukrainian assault groups have now entered the centre of Zarichne and are working to clear the remaining residential areas from multiple different directions.
Additionally, multiple Ukrainian assault groups managed to cross the Zherebets River and enter the centre of Torske, while other small groups managed to infiltrate even further east of the village. Individual Ukrainian infiltration groups are now moving east towards the border with Luhansk Oblast, south along the eastern bank of the Zherebets River towards Yampil, and north towards the northern part of Torske.
To the south, Russian forces launched a new series of deep infiltration operations, exploiting the lack of positions in the large forests southeast of Lyman. Several small assault groups managed reach the northern outskirts of Dibrova and the nearby summer camps, while others reached the eastern outskirts of Lyman in the area of the railway line. Individual Russian DRG groups are also operating near the southern and eastern streets of Lyman.…

Situation on the Borova direction, Kharkiv/Luhansk Oblast:
Over the last two weeks, Ukrainian forces continued their coordinated series of counterattacks northeast of Borova, where they made new advances in two different areas.
In the southeast, Ukrainian forces cleared the fields north of Novoiehorivka, advancing east through the forested areas towards Kovalivka. Assault operations east of Nadiya towards the village of Raihorodka are also taking place.
To the northwest, Ukrainian forces expanded their counterattacks to the Stepy area, re-establishing full control over the village, as well as the surroundings of Kopanky. Fighting continues for the Vyshneve area, where Ukrainian forces are attempting to infiltrate the village and the fields to the north.
+ ~6.23 km² in favour of Ukraine.

Situation on the Yunakivka direction, Sumy Oblast:
Over the last couple of weeks, Ukrainian forces have continued their coordinated series of counterattacks, making important advances in and around the tactically-significant town of Yunakivka.
After re-establishing control over the southern streets of Yunakivka, Ukrainian forces went on to recapture the town centre, western streets, and eastern streets, driving the Russians back to the northern outskirts. The northern part of Yunakivka remains in a contested grey-zone, with mixed and overlapping positions being held by each side, however Ukraine seemingly has an advantage in this area and is completing their clearing operations to officially re-establish control over the town.
East and west of Yunakivka, limited counterattacks and clearing operations are also taking place. Ukrainian forces cleared parts of the forests north of Stavky, and are infiltrating west along the highway west of Yunakivka. Further west, the situation has stabilised for Russia after Ukraine regained control over all of the forests north of Sumy City last month.
+ ~4.21 km² in favour of Ukraine.

Situation on the Hlukhiv direction, Sumy Oblast:
Over the last couple of weeks, positional battles continued in border regions of the Hlukhiv direction, where Ukrainian forces managed to make marginal advances.
Ukrainian forces continued their clearing operations against the remaining Russian positions in Bachivsk, and, after recapturing the central part of the settlement, they managed to dislodge the Russians from the northeastern streets, thereby re-establishing full control over the village. Meanwhile, sporadic fighting and assault operations continue in the treelines to the southeast of Bachivsk, without any significant frontline changes.
+ ~1.09 km² in favour of Ukraine.

1/ Why is the Russian media constantly reporting the capture of Ukrainian towns and villages, while in reality the frontline is mostly frozen? It's because "treason, cowardice, and deceit are all around," complains a Russian warblogger, quoting Tsar Nicholas II. ⬇️

thread.text: 2/ Yuri Kotenok raises a question he says is constantly being asked by his readers: "practically every week there are reports of villages being liberated in one direction or another, but the front line is largely at a standstill. Why?"

3/ "Firstly, we are, indeed, recapturing some villages for an encore, in the sense that they periodically come under our or their control. This is war, and it's a seesaw. In many areas of the front line, there are head-on battles.
4/ "Considering that the enemy has excellent communications, decent armour, and is pushing FPV, they sometimes succeed. We are recapturing them—it's a seesaw.
5/ "The second reason is, in my opinion, the main one. The fact is, a classic front line, as understood in past conflicts, no longer exists.

6/ "Positions outside populated areas are typically separated by kilometres, sometimes even 10-15, and in between lies the notorious kill zone (official media still shy away from using the term) or grey zone, where, roughly speaking, anything that moves is exposed to fire.

7/ "In villages, hamlets, and towns, the enemy may even be within sight, but the challenge for each side is rotating positions and bringing in ammunition and food, because routes are being targeted, routed, and mined from the air.
8/ "Both we and the enemy are increasingly being supplied by air. The Ukrainians are even evacuating the wounded by helicopter [actually heavy drones].

9/ "Now, about liberation and control itself—an entry into a populated area by a raid/assault/reconnaissance group and an attempt to consolidate there (which can sometimes be unsuccessful, because there's a war going on) is often passed off as the liberation of the village:…

10/ …"We've entered! There's the flag! There's the administration building! We've taken it! It's ours! We've secured it!" And what happens next? Again, there's no information about that, because it's already a matter of discretion.
11/ "Then it's the same old up-and-down process: they push us out, we push back, we manoeuvre, sometimes in the opposite direction, if we're still alive.
12/ "But reports are then sent up the chain of command from groups/squads/platoons/companies/battalions, reaching the level of brigades/divisions/army groups, and so on up to the General Staff.

13/ "This is how maps with colouring are prepared. From there, reports on the offensive are sent to the highest offices.
In my opinion, this is how reality is distorted, and misinformation is layered on top of the command and government leadership.

14/ "It's nothing personal, it's just the system. This practice has developed in recent years. I won't even cite examples—they've been around for YEARS. The situation isn't changing, despite official reports that towns and villages have been liberated, and repeatedly.

15/ "Why is this being done? To generate publicity, to create a positive image, to present information in a positive light. But the result is a clear disproportion and distortion—the case suffers because reality doesn't match what exists on paper and in the media.

16/ "And it is precisely on these "pillars" that the entire awards system and career advancement in the security forces are based.
The words from the diary of the last Russian emperor, Nicholas II, come to mind: 'Treason, cowardice, and deceit are all around.'"

17/ "They were said in a different era and apply to a different political situation. But as for deception, it seems to me that we're once again close to world records. I'd add to the traditional domestic ills nepotism, which has simply engulfed our power structures.

18/ "And regarding treason, I'll say this: given the speed with which information flows from our headquarters to those same overseas "partners," and the rampant enemy agents who have launched a hunt for our military and civilians in our own rear,…

19/ …this, a century later, is once again a major problem for Russia." /end

Who else dies in Russia's war.
The leaked death register records where each man was born, not his citizenship, but that is enough to find the foreigners.
Of the 429,622 war deaths in my count, 732 were born outside the former Soviet Union. Cubans and Colombians lead, then Nepalis, then men from Nigeria, Yemen, Cameroon, Egypt, China, Iraq, Sri Lanka, Kenya and Ghana: 50 countries in all.
Their number grows every year: 55 died in 2023, 138 in 2024, 357 in 2025 and 181 in 2026 so far, with 2026 still being registered. The Nepalis died mostly in 2023, the Colombians and most of the Africans in 2025 and 2026.
A foreign recruit gets a Russian death record only if someone registers his death in Russia, and many never will.
Closer to home the numbers are larger. 3,786 men were born after 1991 in Central Asia, the Caucasus, Belarus, Moldova or the Baltic states, most likely migrants who took Russian passports. 15,763 more were born there in Soviet times. 19,886 were born in Ukraine, four in five of them in the areas Russia now occupies.
Three in four were born in Russia, and 15% of the records give no place of birth.

People doubt the leaked Russian death register: wrong causes of death, people counted twice, civilians. So I checked every act behind my count, and here is its strictest reading. Only deaths whose record carries the war code Y36, "operations of war", count.
My count, used in all my posts, is 429,622 war deaths (the site itself counts 440,982). 333,419 of them are coded Y36. Only men of 18 to 59, with clear errors removed: 331,163.
Where the difference goes:
Combat or missing in action without a Y36 code, 76,834. The record describes the war in words, a court has declared a missing man dead, or the death type says "during military action", but the code field is empty.
Non-combat deaths, 12,287. Heart disease, cancer, suicide, road crashes. These are the "wrong causes" people point at.
No cause on the record, 3,342, mostly Russian residents who died in the occupied areas.
Should not count, 3,740: the same death written twice, deaths before the invasion, and terror attacks such as Crocus City Hall.
Among the Y36 acts, 1,197 women, people over 60 and children, mostly in Russia's border oblasts, and 1,059 double acts, deaths abroad and deaths before the war.
So 331,163 is a floor, not a new estimate.

thread.text:
So what are the 96,203 deaths in my count without a Y36 code? I decoded every act by what its record says.
Combat or missing in action: 76,834, four in five. About 41,600 records describe an explosion, shelling, a mine or a drone in words, and 3,230 a gunshot. 6,269 name the war in general words. 18,127 are court decisions declaring missing men dead: no body, so no medical cause and no code. 5,388 carry only the death type "during military action", and 1,410 died later of war wounds.
These men look exactly like the Y36 dead. The median age is 39 against 38, and women are 0.1% in both groups. They died in the same front-line villages, from Robotyne and Bakhmut to Klishchiivka and Kreminna. On their records the code field is usually just blank or holds the placeholder 99999.
Non-combat: 12,287. Disease, suicide, crashes, violence. Armies count such deaths as losses, but these records cannot show who served: almost half died far from the war, and 5% are women.
No cause at all: 3,342, mostly Russian residents who died in the occupied areas. By age and sex they look like the rest: almost all men, few over 60.
Should not count: 3,740. 1,831 repeat another act, 1,422 died before the invasion, and 487 died in terror attacks such as Crocus City Hall.

What the Y36 deaths are. 90% are coded as explosions and fragments, the rest mostly unspecified or firearms.
The odd codes are few. 3 acts say nuclear weapons and 72 biological weapons; their own wording says explosions, so a digit was mistyped. Naval, chemical and "after hostilities ended" add 481, again mostly explosions by their wording. Only 8 of the 333,419 Y36 acts name a disease as the cause of death.

The errors that matter are small. 964 acts look like a second act for the same person: same birth date, sex and death date, and the same certificate or birthplace. 90 died in Mali, Syria and the Central African Republic: Russian forces abroad, not the war in Ukraine. 5 are dated before the invasion. Together 1,059 acts, 0.3%.
One date problem is bigger but leaves the deaths in place. 8,147 acts have a death certificate dated before the stated death, mostly by up to three weeks. It is rare until 2025, then suddenly common from February to May 2025, at its peak one act in eight that month. Those deaths may sit a few weeks late in a monthly chart.

Who is left. Five in six died in Ukraine, at the front line and in occupied towns. For one in eleven the place is not given, mostly in 2022 and 2023 acts. The rest died in Russia's border oblasts, mostly in the Kursk fighting, or in Moscow, St Petersburg and Rostov, where the military hospitals are.
They look like soldiers. The median age is 38, and eight in ten are 24 to 51. Women are 0.2% of Y36 deaths in Ukraine. Shelling kills women as well as men, so few women means few civilians: even at three civilian men for each civilian woman, civilian men would be about 1,500 of the 331,163.
What the record cannot say is who served where. The army, Rosgvardia, private military companies, prisoners recruited to fight and the Donetsk and Luhansk corps look the same in a death act.

What this means. Read in the strictest way, my count holds 331,163 Russian war deaths to 28 August 2026. With the combat and missing deaths that only lack the code, it is about 408,000. 2026 is still being registered. The errors critics find are real, but they move the count by a few percent.
The register misses what never reached it: soldiers missing without a court decision, and bodies never recovered. So every count from it is a floor for Russia's losses, not a total.
I'm sure @cpartisans have given @mediazona_en enough data for their next update, and other analysts will publish their own reports soon.

This will be my last post based on the data I've examined, at least until the official dataset is properly explained and made public.
My analysis is incomplete and may miss important details. I'd recommend waiting for established media outlets and independent investigators to publish their findings before drawing firm conclusions.

desk.text:
I now have the data to reevaluate my previous estimates, so why not?
Until 2024, Mediazona and the leaked Russian death register match almost month by month. From 2025, Mediazona starts falling behind. By late 2025, it has recorded only about a third of the deaths already in the register.
By the end of 2025, the leaked register itself also starts falling behind, as the confirmation lag catches up with it. The names aren't necessarily missing. They're just slow to appear.
So I revised my GSUA ratios to fit the register: from 1:4.5 in 2022–23 down to 1:2 since February 2025.
On the chart, the black line is GSUA adjusted by those ratios, and the dashed line is the register. They track each other closely until the register's recent months start filling in.
At these ratios, Mediazona's list should eventually reach around 607,000 names.
There is still room for refinement. Early Mediazona figures exceed the projected values, while SBS statistics suggest the KIA ratio may fall further in 2026. So I expect the final estimate to land somewhere between 580,000 and 620,000 dead.
Even if the leaked dataset is fake, it's still useful to know what the other side estimates. You are free to disagree with those numbers, but they're worth examining.

thread.text:
The leaked Russian death register has one number that barely moves: deaths confirmed within a month.
From late 2023 to mid-2026, about 3 000 to 4 800 war deaths were confirmed within 30 days, month after month. Meanwhile the monthly total grew from about 6 000 to over 18 000.
Look at the lightest part of the bars: it stays about the same height while everything above it grows. That looks like a system working at full capacity: recovering bodies, identifying them, issuing the papers. Whatever does not fit into that month waits, for six months, a year, sometimes longer.
In 2022, 78% of war deaths fit into the first month. In 2025, only 24%.
It also means the latest months will always look low. The first 3 500 or so show up fast. The rest come months later.

This analysis is far from complete and may miss many important details. Treat the numbers as preliminary estimates, not established facts.
I'd recommend waiting for proper media outlets and independent investigators to publish their own reports before drawing firm conclusions.
Follow @cpartisans for the updates

desk.text:
I compared the leaked Russian death register with UALosses, battle by battle. The Russian register records where each soldier died, so both sides can be placed on the same map.
Russia lost more soldiers than Ukraine in every battle but one.*
Pokrovsk: 4.7 Russian dead for every Ukrainian loss. Siversk 3.9, Avdiivka 3.4, Kostiantynivka 3.0, Toretsk 2.6.
The closest ratios came from offensives Ukraine launched: Robotyne 0.9, Velyka Novosilka 1.2, Kursk and Sumy 1.3. Robotyne, the 2023 counteroffensive, is the only battle where the Ukrainian count exceeds the Russian one.
And these aren't even equal measures. The Russian register counts confirmed deaths only. UALosses includes killed, missing and captured. The actual gap may be wider.
Both datasets are cut off at December 2025, because Russian deaths can take months to appear in the register. That's why Pokrovsk shows 15.8k here, rather than the 21.5k in my earlier post. Kursk includes the fighting in Sumy oblast.
*Most Russian deaths recorded in 2023 have no location of death, making the Robotyne comparison particularly incomplete.

Based on the available Rosstat data, here is the confirmation lag: how long it takes from a war death to the death certificate.
Median time from death to certificate:
Died in 2023: 15 days
Died in 2024: 52 days
Died in 2025: 126 days, about 4 months
Declared dead by a court (MIA): 316 days
Certified within 30 days of death: 60% of 2023 deaths, 42% of 2024, 26% of 2025.
The process gets slower every year. A death in 2025 took about eight times longer to be confirmed than one in 2023. Those declared dead by a court wait most of a year, many of them longer.
This is why the latest months always look low in Russian registry data: most of the dead are not in the register yet. A month of deaths is close to complete only about a year later.

thread.text:
Was Kursk different from other battles?
Per month, it was one of the most intense of the war: 948 Ukrainian records a month from Aug 2024 to May 2025, behind only Mariupol (1,084) and Bakhmut (1,034), ahead of Pokrovsk (768).
Per area it was the cheapest: 4.9 records for each km² that changed hands, against 13.1 at Pokrovsk, 19.7 at Avdiivka and 36.9 at Chasiv Yar. It was a war of movement, with about 1,900 km² taken and lost in ten months, while the siege battles ground over a few km² for months.
The status of its records is typical for 2024–25 battles: 57% are MIA and 5% POW. The losses were high in time, not in ground.

Kursk and the rest of the front
Ukraine held up to 902 km² of Kursk oblast in Aug–Sep 2024 and lost almost all of it by spring 2025. Inside Ukraine, Russia gained 2,678 km² in the operation's first six months, against 889 km² in the six months before, and Ukrainian losses there stayed about the same (24.4k against 22.7k records), so the Kursk losses came on top.
After Kursk fell, the fighting moved into Sumy oblast. Ukrainian records of loss there rose from 727 (Aug 2024 – Feb 2025) to 6,036 (Mar – Dec 2025), and Russia took about 260 km² of the oblast.
Leaving Kursk did not bring Ukrainian losses down. They averaged 4,990 records a month during the operation (Aug 2024 – Feb 2025) and 4,640 after it (Mar – Dec 2025), against 3,790 before it. The border fighting simply moved from Kursk into Sumy oblast.

Was the rise just Russia scaling up its war?
Russia did fight harder during the operation: the General Staff's count of Russian killed and wounded rose 31% (32.1k to 42.1k a month, Kursk included), and Russian gains inside Ukraine went from 148 to 415 km² a month.
Yet Ukrainian losses on the rest of the front barely moved: 3,742, 3,815 and 3,810 a month before, during and after. The extra Ukrainian losses were on the border: 44 a month before, 1,175 during, 832 after.

Would these losses have come anyway?
Partly. When Russia attacked across the border into Kharkiv oblast in May 2024, Ukrainian records of loss there rose from 265 to 839 a month (Feb–Apr against May–Jul 2024). After Kursk, the defence of Sumy oblast cost 604 a month.
So a Russian border offensive would likely have cost Ukraine something like 570–600 records a month.
During the operation the border cost 1,175 a month, about twice that: on these numbers about 4,000 records, roughly 40% of the Kursk total, were the extra price of holding ground inside Russia.
This is a counterfactual, not a measurement: a Russian autumn offensive could have been larger than the Kharkiv one.
A gamble that didn't pay off.
One of its aims was to draw Russian forces away from Donbas. Instead Russia brought in thousands of North Korean troops to fight in Kursk and kept pressing in Donbas, where its advance sped up. Ukraine kept no ground in Russia, and the fighting moved onto its own territory in Sumy oblast.
here is Kursk operation recap

A follow-up on Kursk.
The UALosses Kursk category shows 18.6k dead, missing and captured. That matches Kursk and Sumy oblasts together since August 2024, and only 9.9k of them are in Kursk oblast itself.
The rest is the real story. The battle never ended, it just moved.
Operation: 1,175 losses a month
Collapse: 1,150 a month. Ukraine was pushed out of Kursk, and the losses didn't even drop
Sumy: 707 a month, now almost all of it on Ukrainian soil

New details on the aftermath of the September 12 strike on the Togliattikauchuk plant
On September 12, Ukrainian Defense Forces struck the Togliattikauchuk petrochemical plant, whose products can be used in the production chain of components for solid rocket propellants.
Earlier, the Telegram channel "Absolutely Reliable Source" identified damage to the BK-2, BK-3, and BK-4 production units. Meanwhile, additional satellite imagery allowed me to identify repair cranes near the D-4 hydrocarbon separation unit, which uses extractive distillation.
The unit's primary function is to separate and purify 1,3-butadiene from C4 hydrocarbon mixtures through extractive distillation. Butadiene is used in the production of synthetic rubber, automotive tires, ABS plastics, and other polymers.
Certain butadiene-derived polymers are also used as binders in solid rocket propellants. However, the presence of repair cranes near the D-4 unit does not, by itself, confirm that the unit was damaged.

The 7th Corps of the Ukrainian Air Assault Forces has taken over the Huliaipole direction as its area of responsibility.
This is one of the most critical sectors of the entire front. Here is why.
1. The road to Zaporizhzhia.
Huliaipole is less than 100 km from Zaporizhzhia, a city of strategic importance for the whole of southern Ukraine. The russian army sees Huliaipole as a staging ground for further offensive operations toward Zaporizhzhia. If the enemy gains a foothold here, it gains a springboard to push deeper into the region.
2. A hub for massing forces.
Urban environment allows the enemy to concentrate personnel and equipment, set up command posts, deploy artillery positions and establish launch sites for drone operators, all under cover of existing infrastructure. A town in enemy hands is a base from which offensive operations are prepared and sustained.
3. Logistical Node.
